speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you are an infant presenting with recurrent stridor and wheezing; to help me understand your condition, can you tell me exactly when these breathing difficulties occur, such as during feeding or crying?

speaker: Patient
text: 10-month-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes of stridor and wheezing. The mother notes that the wheezing exacerbates when the child is crying, feeding, and when his neck is flexed. Additionally, there are instances where the child vomits after feeding.

speaker: Doctor
text: Based on the exacerbation of symptoms with neck flexion (the "steal" sign) and vomiting, I suspect a structural abnormality. REQUEST TEST: Lateral_Neck_XRay and REQUEST IMAGES: Upper_Airway_Series. Can you confirm if these symptoms started immediately after birth or developed gradually?

OBSERVATION_ATTACK.clean_observation: RESULTS: The symptoms and physical findings (stridor worsening with neck flexion, feeding difficulties, and vomiting) in this 10-month-old are highly suggestive of a congenital vascular ring, specifically a double aortic arch. These structural anomalies are present at birth but often present gradually or become symptomatic as the infant grows and gains weight, rather than causing immediate severe distress right after delivery in all cases. The "steal" sign (worsening of stridor with neck flexion) and the vomiting episodes are classic indicators of external compression of the trachea and esophagus by the vascular ring. The imaging tests requested (Lateral Neck X-ray and Upper Airway Series) along with the provided data (Chest X-ray, Barium Swallow, Echocardiogram) confirm the presence of tracheal compression, esophageal compression, and the confirmatory diagnosis of a double aortic arch.
